newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia net profit surges in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia net profit surges in 1996.

text.p: Telecom Italia's net profit rose "more than 50 percent" in 1996 to over two trillion lire, the state controlled company said in a statement on Monday.
The firm, which has a virtual monopoly on fixed line operations in Italy, added that turnover on new services rose 70 percent last year by comparison with 1995 figures.
Telecom Italia said total turnover would be around 29.4 trillion lire last year, slightly down from 1995's 30.09 trillion lire.
However the 1995 figures included six months of results from mobile phone operations which were then spun off into a separate unit, Telecom Italia Mobile.
Telecom Italia, which is controlled by telecom holding Stet, said its net debt fell to around 12 trillion lire last year from 14.79 trillion in 1995.
The firm said the jump in profit in 1996 was achieved against a background of sharply lower international and inter-city telephone tariffs.

In 1995, the company reported a net profit of 1.75 trillion lire, but that also included results from the mobile phone business. Telecom said its 1996 results were being compared to the 1995 results stripped of the mobile operations.
Stet and Telecom Italia are due to be merged later this year and slated for privatisation in the autumn of 1997.

"These results follow our financial economic plan...placing Telecom Italia in a positive position from which to confront the privatisation and liberalisation (of the telecoms market)," Telecom managing director Francesco Chirichigno said.
Telecom said that in a bid to cut costs the firm reduced the workforce by some 4,000 people last year to 84,750.

It said the ratio between labour costs and turnover was under 24 percent. "This means Telecom is one of the best telecommunication companies at a world level in terms of efficiency and productivity," Telecom said.
It said industrial investments rose 23.3 percent last year to some 8.2 trillion lire. It added that the extra investment costs were covered by self-financing.
National telephone traffic rose five percent in 1995, while international calls rose around 12 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
